question: Which among the following is west flowing river and drain into Arabian Sea?
solution:
The correct answer is Narmada.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

**Among the options provided, the Narmada river is the west flowing river that drains into the Arabian Sea. **

__
 
• The Narmada river is one of the major rivers in India and flows through the states of Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Gujarat.
 
• It originates from the Amarkantak Plateau in Madhya Pradesh and flows westward, eventually draining into the Arabian Sea.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****The Narmada River is a west flowing river in India that drains into the Arabian Sea.**

 
• It originates from the Amarkantak Plateau in the eastern part of Madhya Pradesh, near the border with Chhattisgarh.
 
• From there, it flows in a generally westward direction, traversing through Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Gujarat.
 
• The Narmada River is known for its scenic beauty and plays a significant role in the economy and culture of the regions it passes through
 
• . It is one of the longest rivers in India, with a length of approximately 1,312 kilometers (815 miles).
 
• As the Narmada River flows westward, it eventually reaches the Gulf of Khambhat, which is part of the Arabian Sea.
 
• The river forms an estuary near Bharuch in Gujarat, where it meets the sea.
 
• The estuary is an ecologically important area that supports a diverse range of flora and fauna.
 
• The Narmada River and its basin have considerable importance for irrigation, hydropower generation, and drinking water supply.
 
• Several dams and reservoirs have been built along the river, including the Sardar Sarovar Dam, which is one of the largest dams in India.

In summary, the Narmada River is the west flowing river among the options provided, and it drains into the Arabian Sea. It originates in Madhya Pradesh and flows through Maharashtra and Gujarat before reaching its estuary near Bharuch.
